subject: bio
source: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) syllabus for examination in 2026, 2027 and 2028 — Cambridge International; Year 10 covers topics 1–13 (first half of the two-year course)

weeks.topic: Characteristics of living organisms
objectives: Describe the seven characteristics of living organisms
Define movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion and nutrition

weeks.topic: Classification: the binomial system and dichotomous keys
objectives: Explain how organisms are classified into groups by shared features
Use the binomial system of naming species
Construct and use dichotomous keys

weeks.topic: Features of organisms: the five kingdoms, vertebrates, arthropods and viruses
objectives: Describe the main features of the animal, plant, fungus, prokaryote and protoctist kingdoms
Identify the five vertebrate classes and four arthropod groups
Describe the structure of a virus

weeks.topic: Cell structure: animal, plant and bacterial cells
objectives: Identify cell structures in animal, plant and bacterial cells
State the functions of the nucleus, cytoplasm, membrane, cell wall, chloroplast and ribosomes

weeks.topic: Specialised cells, tissues, organs and organ systems
objectives: Relate the structure of specialised cells to their functions
Define tissue, organ and organ system with examples

weeks.topic: Size of specimens: magnification and microscopy
objectives: Use the formula magnification = image size / actual size
Convert between millimetres and micrometres
Draw and label specimens seen under a microscope

weeks.topic: Diffusion
objectives: Define diffusion as net movement down a concentration gradient
Investigate factors that affect the rate of diffusion
Explain the importance of diffusion in living organisms

weeks.topic: Osmosis and water potential in plant tissues
objectives: Define osmosis in terms of water potential and a partially permeable membrane
Investigate osmosis using potato or dialysis tubing
Explain turgor, plasmolysis and flaccidity in plant cells

weeks.topic: Active transport
objectives: Define active transport as movement against a concentration gradient using energy
Describe the role of protein carriers
Give examples such as ion uptake by root hair cells

weeks.topic: Biological molecules: carbohydrates, fats, proteins and DNA
objectives: List the chemical elements in carbohydrates, fats and proteins
Name the smaller molecules each large molecule is made from
Describe the double-helix structure of DNA and base pairing

weeks.topic: Food tests: iodine, Benedict's, biuret, ethanol emulsion and DCPIP
objectives: Carry out tests for starch, reducing sugars, proteins and fats
Use DCPIP to test for vitamin C
Record and interpret positive and negative results

weeks.topic: Enzymes as biological catalysts: the lock-and-key model
objectives: Define catalyst and enzyme
Explain enzyme action using active site and substrate complementarity
Describe the enzyme–substrate complex

weeks.topic: Enzymes: effects of temperature and pH
objectives: Investigate the effect of temperature and pH on enzyme activity
Explain denaturation and optimum conditions
Use kinetic energy and collisions to explain rate changes

weeks.topic: Photosynthesis: equations and uses of glucose
objectives: State word and balanced symbol equations for photosynthesis
Describe the role of chlorophyll in transferring light energy
Describe how plants use and store the glucose made

weeks.topic: Review: cells, movement into and out of cells, biological molecules and enzymes
objectives: Revisit cell structure, magnification and transport across membranes
Practise food test and enzyme exam questions

weeks.topic: Limiting factors of photosynthesis and investigations
objectives: Investigate light intensity, carbon dioxide and temperature effects on photosynthesis
Interpret limiting factor graphs
Use hydrogencarbonate indicator to show gas exchange in plants

weeks.topic: Leaf structure and mineral requirements
objectives: Identify leaf tissues and relate them to photosynthesis
Explain the importance of nitrate and magnesium ions
Describe deficiency symptoms in plants

weeks.topic: Human nutrition: balanced diet and deficiency diseases
objectives: Describe a balanced diet and the roles of each nutrient
Explain causes of scurvy and rickets
Relate dietary needs to age, activity and pregnancy

weeks.topic: The digestive system: organs and functions
objectives: Identify the organs of the alimentary canal and associated organs
Describe ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation and egestion

weeks.topic: Physical digestion: teeth, the stomach and the role of bile
objectives: Identify types of human teeth and their functions
Describe how bile emulsifies fats
Explain the role of hydrochloric acid in the stomach

weeks.topic: Chemical digestion and absorption: enzymes and villi
objectives: Describe the action of amylase, protease and lipase
Explain how villi and microvilli increase absorption
Describe the role of the small intestine in absorbing water

weeks.topic: Transport in plants: xylem and phloem
objectives: Identify the positions of xylem and phloem in roots, stems and leaves
Relate xylem structure to water transport and support

weeks.topic: Water uptake and transpiration
objectives: Describe the pathway of water from root hair cells to leaves
Investigate factors affecting the rate of transpiration
Explain wilting and the transpiration pull

weeks.topic: Translocation: sources and sinks
objectives: Define translocation of sucrose and amino acids in phloem
Explain how parts of a plant act as sources or sinks at different times

weeks.topic: Circulatory systems: single and double circulation
objectives: Describe the circulatory system of a fish
Explain the advantages of double circulation in mammals

weeks.topic: The heart: structure, function and coronary heart disease
objectives: Label the chambers, valves and major blood vessels of the heart
Investigate the effect of exercise on heart rate
Describe risk factors for coronary heart disease

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: topics 1–9 (living organisms to the heart)
objectives: Complete timed papers on content taught so far
Identify weak areas from marked papers

weeks.topic: Blood vessels: arteries, veins and capillaries
objectives: Relate the structure of arteries, veins and capillaries to their functions
Name the main blood vessels to and from the heart, lungs, liver and kidneys

weeks.topic: Blood: components and functions
objectives: Identify red and white blood cells in photomicrographs
State the functions of plasma, platelets, phagocytes and lymphocytes
Describe blood clotting

weeks.topic: Diseases and immunity: pathogens, transmission and body defences
objectives: Define pathogen and transmissible disease
Describe ways pathogens are transmitted
Explain body defences including skin, mucus and stomach acid

weeks.topic: Antibodies, active and passive immunity and vaccination
objectives: Explain how antibodies and memory cells give active immunity
Describe the role of vaccination in controlling disease
Compare active and passive immunity

weeks.topic: Gas exchange in humans: gas exchange surfaces and breathing
objectives: Describe the features of gas exchange surfaces
Explain the role of intercostal muscles and diaphragm in ventilation
Compare inspired and expired air

weeks.topic: Aerobic respiration
objectives: State the word and balanced equations for aerobic respiration
Describe uses of energy in the body
Investigate the effect of temperature on respiration in yeast or seeds

weeks.topic: Anaerobic respiration in humans and yeast
objectives: State equations for anaerobic respiration in muscles and yeast
Explain oxygen debt and lactic acid removal after exercise

weeks.topic: Excretion in humans: the kidneys and the liver
objectives: Describe the structure and function of the kidney and nephron
Explain the role of the liver in deamination and urea formation

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: topics 1–13
objectives: Complete end-of-year papers covering all Year 10 content
Apply data-handling and practical skills to unfamiliar contexts

weeks.topic: Review: transport in animals, disease, gas exchange, respiration and excretion
objectives: Correct errors from end-of-year exams
Consolidate key definitions before Year 11
